literal: At the start of Yuanxiang he was appointed Governor of Western Xia Province and Great Commander for the province; for his cumulative merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Anwu County with a fief of four hundred households.
idiomatic: At the start of Yuanxiang he was made governor of Western Xia Province and great commander for the province; for merit accumulated over many campaigns he was enfeoffed baron of Anwu County with a fief of four hundred households.

literal: He was transferred to act as Governor of You Province.
idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as acting governor of You Province.

literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in attacking the Zhou Emperor Wen at Mang Mountain, besieging Yubi and assaulting Longmen.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in attacking Yuwen Tai at Mang Mountain, besieging Yubi and storming Longmen.

literal: On their return he was left to garrison Jin Province.
idiomatic: On the return march he was left to garrison Jin Province.

literal: When Emperor Wenxuan received the abdication he remained governor; wherever he served, exaction was his chief concern, and officials and commoners resented him.
idiomatic: When Gao Yang received the mandate, Zhang Baoluo remained governor — and wherever he held office, exaction was his chief business. Officials and commoners alike resented him.

literal: At the start of the Jinan reign he was sent out as Governor of Cang Province and enfeoffed Prince of Fucheng Commandery.
idiomatic: At the start of the Jinan reign he was sent out as governor of Cang Province and enfeoffed prince of Fucheng Commandery.

literal: For exactions while in the province he was dismissed from office and stripped of his princely rank.
idiomatic: For squeezing the province dry he was dismissed from office and stripped of his princely rank.

literal: At his death he was posthumously granted his former office and his original enfeoffment was restored.
idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously granted his former office, and his original enfeoffment was restored.

literal: His son Moyan succeeded him.
idiomatic: His son Moyan succeeded him.

literal: At the end of Wuping he was Guard General.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he held the post of guard general.

literal: Those who as tent guards followed the Grand Ancestor east into Shandong included Qu Zhen, Duan Chen, Die Shele, Wei Biao, Qifu Guihe and his brother Linghe, and Wang Kede — all of whom rose to high office through military merit.
idiomatic: Others who as tent guards followed Gao Huan east into Shandong included Qu Zhen, Duan Chen, Die Shele, Wei Biao, Qifu Guihe and his brother Linghe, and Wang Kede — all of whom rose to high office on military merit alone.

literal: Qu Zhen, styled Sheluo, was a native of Jiuquan in Xiping.
idiomatic: Qu Zhen, styled Sheluo, was a native of Jiuquan in Xiping.

literal: Bold and brave, he was skilled in riding and archery.
idiomatic: Bold and brave, he was skilled in riding and archery.

literal: As a tent guard he followed the Grand Ancestor at Jin Province, then joined the uprising and campaigned wherever sent.
idiomatic: As a tent guard he followed Gao Huan at Jin Province, then joined the uprising and fought wherever the army was sent.

literal: At the end of Wuding he was enfeoffed Baron of Fuping County.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was enfeoffed baron of Fuping County.

literal: At the start of Tianbao he drew income from Liyang Commandery and was appointed Governor of Jin Province.
idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao he drew income from Liyang Commandery and was appointed governor of Jin Province.

literal: At the start of Wuping he was transferred to Circuit Executive of Yuzhou, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yuzhou; at death he was posthumously granted Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: At the start of Wuping he was transferred to circuit executive of Yuzhou, director of the Masters of Writing, and governor of Yuzhou; at his death he was posthumously granted grand commandant.

literal: Duan Chen, styled Huaibao, was a native of Dai.
idiomatic: Duan Chen, styled Huaibao, was a native of Dai.

literal: From youth he had martial capacity.
idiomatic: From youth he had real martial capacity.

literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in raising righteousness at Xindu.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in raising righteousness at Xindu.

literal: In the Tianbao era he was Governor of Guang Province.
idiomatic: In the Tianbao era he served as governor of Guang Province.

literal: Die Shele held opening-establishment honor equal to the three excellencies as Governor of Ying Province under Emperor Wucheng, and was enfeoffed Duke of Hanzhong Commandery.
idiomatic: Die Shele, under Emperor Wucheng, held opening-establishment honor equal to the three excellencies as governor of Ying Province and was enfeoffed duke of Hanzhong Commandery.

literal: He died in battle in Guanzhong.
idiomatic: He fell in battle in Guanzhong.

literal: Wei Biao was a native of Dai.
idiomatic: Wei Biao was a native of Dai.

literal: At the start of Daning he was enfeoffed Prince of Haichang.
idiomatic: At the start of Daning he was enfeoffed prince of Haichang.

literal: His son Xianggui succeeded him.
idiomatic: His son Xianggui succeeded him.

literal: Xianggui, at the end of Wuping, was Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Jin Province Circuit Executive and Governor of Jin Province.
idiomatic: Xianggui, at the end of Wuping, was vice director of the Masters of Writing on the Jin Province circuit executive and governor of Jin Province.

literal: Circuit Executive Left Assistant Hou Ziqin and others secretly reported to Emperor Wu of Zhou requesting troops; Ziqin and the rest served as inside agents.
idiomatic: Circuit executive left assistant Hou Ziqin and others secretly reported to Emperor Wu of Zhou, asking that troops be sent; Ziqin and his fellows were to serve as inside agents.

literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou personally led his host to the city walls; at night Ziqin and the others opened the gates and brought the army in, bound Xianggui, and sent him to Chang'an.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou personally led his host to the walls. That night Ziqin and the others opened the gates and admitted the army, bound Xianggui, and sent him to Chang'an.

literal: He soon died.
idiomatic: He soon died.

literal: His younger brother Xiangyuan was forceful and possessed courage and stratagem.
idiomatic: His younger brother Xiangyuan was forceful, with courage and stratagem to match.

literal: At the end of Wuping he was Army-leading Grand General.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was army-leading grand general.

literal: From Pingyang to Bingzhou, and again when he reached Ye, he repeatedly plotted to kill Gao Anagong, depose the Later Sovereign, and set up the Prince of Guangning — but in the end the plan came to nothing.
idiomatic: From Pingyang to Bingzhou, and again on reaching Ye, he repeatedly plotted to kill Gao Anagong, depose the Later Sovereign, and set up the Prince of Guangning — yet in the end the plan came to nothing.

literal: When the Prince of Guangning was sent away, Xiangyuan drew his belt-knife, struck a pillar, and sighed: "The great cause is lost — what more is there to say!"
idiomatic: When the Prince of Guangning was sent away, Xiangyuan drew his belt-knife, struck a pillar, and sighed: "The great cause is lost — what more is there to say!"

literal: The brothers Qifu Guihe and Linghe, at the end of Wuping, both held opening-establishment honor equal to the three excellencies.
idiomatic: The brothers Qifu Guihe and Linghe, at the end of Wuping, both held opening-establishment honor equal to the three excellencies.

literal: Linghe was General Who Leads the Army.
idiomatic: Linghe was general who leads the army.

literal: Before Bingzhou fell, he, together with Army-leading Grand General Han Jianye and Martial Guard Grand General Feng Fuxiang, successively defected to the Zhou army.
idiomatic: Before Bingzhou fell, he, together with army-leading grand general Han Jianye and martial guard grand general Feng Fuxiang, defected one after another to the Zhou army.

literal: Linghe was granted Pillar of State and enfeoffed Duke of Xihe Commandery.
idiomatic: Linghe was granted pillar of state and enfeoffed duke of Xihe Commandery.

literal: At the start of Daye under Sui he died while serving as commander-in-chief at Qin Province.
idiomatic: At the start of Daye under Sui he died while serving as commander-in-chief at Qin Province.

literal: Jianye and Fuxiang — neither is known for certain whence they came.
idiomatic: Jianye and Fuxiang — of neither is it known for certain whence they came.

literal: Jianye was granted Supreme Pillar of State and enfeoffed Duke of the State of Xun; he died in the Kaihuang era of Sui.
idiomatic: Jianye was granted supreme pillar of state and enfeoffed duke of the state of Xun; he died in the Kaihuang era of Sui.

literal: Fuxiang was Supreme Pillar of State and enfeoffed a commandery duke.
idiomatic: Fuxiang was supreme pillar of state and enfeoffed a commandery duke.

literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Bingzhou, he was immediately made commander-in-chief at Shuo Province.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Bingzhou, he was immediately made commander-in-chief at Shuo Province.

literal: Wang Kede was a native of Dai.
idiomatic: Wang Kede was a native of Dai.

literal: He successively served as governor of several provinces and as an official of the Masters of Writing in the Bing provincial secretariat, and was enfeoffed Prince of Xincai Commandery.
idiomatic: He served successively as governor of several provinces and as an official in the Bing provincial Masters of Writing, and was enfeoffed prince of Xincai Commandery.

literal: Houmo Chenxiang was a native of Dai.
idiomatic: Houmo Chenxiang was a native of Dai.

literal: His grandfather Fuyui was First Chieftain of Registered Tribal Peoples under Wei.
idiomatic: His grandfather Fuyui was first chieftain of registered tribal peoples under Wei.

literal: His father Huguti was Governor of Shuo Province and Duke of Baishui Commandery.
idiomatic: His father Huguti was governor of Shuo Province and duke of Baishui Commandery.

literal: The historian writes: The Grand Ancestor for generations dwelt in Yun and Dai, known for heroic stature.
idiomatic: The historian writes: Gao Huan for generations dwelt in Yun and Dai, known to all for heroic stature.

literal: Later he passed through the Erzhu clan and his martial renown gradually rose; old friends of town and district ever more deferred to him.
idiomatic: Later he passed through the Erzhu clan, and his martial renown gradually rose — old friends of town and district ever more deferred to him.

literal: He Bayun, separated from his brothers and dwelling in a place of suspicion and distrust, was at first sheltered for old standing — yet in the end did not obtain a good death; compared with Wu's Zhuge Jin and Shu's Zhuge Liang, one knows how shallow or deep a man's capacity and discernment may be.
idiomatic: He Bayun, torn from his brothers and dwelling in a place of suspicion, was at first sheltered for old standing — yet in the end did not obtain a good death. Set beside Wu's Zhuge Jin and Shu's Zhuge Liang, one sees how shallow or deep a man's capacity and discernment may run.

literal: Liu Gui and Cai Jun had foresight; when the hegemonic enterprise was first laid they loyally supported it from deep conviction — to share sacrifice in the Pure Temple was no empty honor.
idiomatic: Liu Gui and Cai Jun had foresight. When the hegemonic enterprise was first laid, they loyally supported it from deep conviction — to share sacrifice in the Pure Temple was no empty honor.

literal: When Han Xian and the rest heard the righteous uprising, they raced to the ranks of war, leaned on reflected glory, and gave their will and strength full play — that they became lords and marquises was only fitting.
idiomatic: When Han Xian and the rest heard the righteous uprising, they raced to the ranks of war, leaned on reflected glory, and gave their will and strength full play — that they rose to become lords and marquises was only fitting.

literal: The encomium says: Among kin of the imperial homeland, each generation has had such men.
idiomatic: The encomium says: Among kin of the imperial homeland, each generation has had such men.

literal: Spirit descended on the Yun-Shuo lands; loyal ministers rose in their season.
idiomatic: Spirit descended on the Yun-Shuo lands; loyal ministers rose in their season.

literal: In the land where merit and fame are won, they stand as neighbors to the ancients.
idiomatic: In the land where merit and fame are won, they stand as neighbors to the ancients.

literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
